newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says over 100 Kurd rebels dead.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says over 100 Kurd rebels dead.

text.p: Turkey said its security forces killed 118 Kurdish guerrillas on Tuesday in clashes that spilled over the mountainous border into northern Iraq.
The regional governor's office said in a statement that eleven members of the security forces had also died in the fighting with Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels.
No independent confirmation of the death toll was immediately available.
Heavy clashes frequently break out in the remote border region. The PKK, fighting for Kurdish self rule, has bases hidden in the remote Turkish mountains and just inside Iraq.

State-run Anatolian news agency said the clashes took place in the southeastern Turkish provinces of Sirnak and Hakkari but security sources told Reuters the troops had attacked PKK rebels entering Turkey from Iraq and then pursued them back across the border where fighting continued.
"F-16 jets have been taking off from Diyarbakir throughout the day," a witness said in the southeastern city.
A local official said earlier that Turkish troops backed by helicopter gunships and fighter-bombers have killed 43 Kurd rebels in a central Turkish province over the last 10 days.
More than 20,000 people have been killed in the 12-year-old conflict.
